steps.title: Definition
steps.body: De-industrialisation is the decline in the importance of the secondary sector (manufacturing) in a country's economy, measured by output or employment.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A post-industrial economy is one where the service sector (tertiary) and knowledge-based industries (quaternary) dominate, having replaced manufacturing as the main source of employment and GDP.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Science parks are located near universities and focus on research and high-tech industries. Business parks are developments offering modern office space for service-sector companies. Both are typically located on the edge of cities where land is cheaper and transport links are good.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: The north-south divide refers to the perceived economic and cultural differences between southern England (wealthier, service-based, London-centric) and northern England (historically industrial, lower average incomes, higher unemployment).

steps.body: Use specific UK examples: Cambridge Science Park, Manchester regeneration, coal mining decline Include data in your answers (percentages, employment figures, GDP contributions) For north-south divide questions, compare specific indicators (wages, unemployment, life expectancy) Always evaluate both positive and negative impacts of economic change Know the difference between tertiary and quaternary sectors For Brexit questions, present a balanced view with both challenges and opportunities Higher mark questions: consider whether government strategies to reduce the divide have been effective
